label: Backup repository
type: a named storage location inside a backup:archive, created via cbbackupmgr's config sub-command and holding one cluster's backups (full and incremental). The SAME construct whether it is written to by the cbbackupmgr CLI directly or by the Backup Service's own plan mechanism - a plan storesDataIn a repository, and cbbackupmgr acquiresLockOn one, per round 11's own already-promoted relation.
recurrence_note: Recurrence recomputed for round 25 at 18 distinct files (relation-slot metric), up from 6/7 at last write. The 12 new files are round 25's rest-api/backup-*.md batch, which was dispatched specifically to test whether this record's central claim - the SAME construct whether written to by cbbackupmgr or the Backup Service's plan mechanism - holds up against the REST surface. It does, and more strongly than before: see the round-25 addendum below.
aliases_note: Round 19's dispatch briefing warned agents not to conflate the Backup SERVICE (cluster-managed, plan-driven) with the cbbackupmgr TOOL (administrator-run CLI) - correctly, for most of what the two do. One batch applied that warning to 'repository' itself and minted backup:cbbackupmgr-repository 'deliberately NOT reused' as the extraction-layer backup:repository, reasoning the tool's repository is a filesystem directory it manages directly while the service's is a plan target. That reasoning turned out to be wrong about THIS term specifically: round 11's own extraction of backup-service.md, already in the registry before round 19 ran, states `tool:cbbackupmgr acquiresLockOn backup:repository` - the tool and the service were already on record as writing into the same kind of repository, and the batch's own registry check (registry-digest.py, which shows labels, not existing relations) could not have surfaced that. A refusal to reuse is only as good as the set it checked, and a concept's existing RELATIONS are part of that set, not just its label. Folded here, 7 files combined (6 for backup:repository, 1 for the now-retired spelling), zero overlap.
round_25_addendum: Round 25 dispatched 22 rest-api/backup-*.md pages specifically to re-test this record's 'SAME construct' claim against the Backup Service's REST API, and the finding holds up, confirmed from three independent angles rather than one: (1) STORAGE - backup-create-repository.md's `archive` parameter definition ('a location on a filesystem, or on a cloud, that is not used for any other repository') matches cbbackupmgr's own archive/repository containment relationship field-for-field, down to the identical `chgrp couchbase` filesystem-permission instruction. (2) ADDRESSING - backup-examine-data.md's `data_path` field ('bucket, scope, and collection... period-separated, e.g. `travel-sample._default._default`') is the IDENTICAL dot-separated format as cbbackupmgr's own `--collection-string` flag (backup:collection-string, promoted this round) - a renamed carrier for one shared addressing model, not a re-derived one. (3) LIFECYCLE - backup-import-repository.md's entire premise (a repository deleted from the Backup Service but still on disk can be re-registered) only makes sense if the repository is a filesystem-durable object independent of either surface's own bookkeeping - the Backup Service's 'delete' is a deregistration, not a destruction. This is round 11's finding CONFIRMED AND EXTENDED at the storage/addressing/lifecycle layer, but round 25 also found what round 11 could not have known to look for: the Backup Service layers a scheduling/policy object (backup:plan, promoted this round) and a three-member task-type taxonomy (BACKUP/MERGE/PRUNE - backup:backup-task/backup:merge-task/backup:prune-task, all promoted this round) on top of the shared repository construct, and cbbackupmgr has no equivalent for either the plan object or the PRUNE task type at all (its closest analogues are a one-shot merge subcommand and a single-backup --remove-backup deletion, not a scheduled policy). So: 'same construct' is correct and now more strongly evidenced for the STORAGE OBJECT specifically; it was never a claim about the whole operational model built on top of it, and round 25's own evidence is what makes that scope explicit for the first time. This is a refining note, not a reversal - the original claim is left standing precisely as worded.
evidence: This directory is referred to as the backup archive. The backup archive contains one or more backup repositories.
A backup repository is created by using the config subcommand.
The `cbbackupmgr` tool takes a lock on the repository to which it's backing up data.
You associate a plan with a repository where it stored backup data.
relates_to_competency_question: Is a backup repository a tool-specific filesystem construct, or the same storage location the Backup Service's own plans write into?
